response.rationale: The patient exhibits classic catatonic signs (echopraxia, mitmachen, mutism, staring) along with progressive decline and psychiatric symptoms. Other candidates are less supported by negative labs and imaging.

rejected.why: No myoclonus, LP negative, MRI not typical for CJD.
B12 is high, homocysteine normal, no deficiency.
TSH normal, so hypothyroid encephalopathy unlikely.
Mirtazapine may cause psychosis but does not explain catatonia.
Delirium is acute, but symptoms are progressive over 3 months.
White matter changes are nonspecific and do not explain catatonia.
Vascular dementia lacks catatonic features and stepwise decline.
DLB requires parkinsonism and typical visual hallucinations; not present.
